beats.say: This is Agentrix WebAgent Platform, by Zavora Technologies. Our entry for the Vultr Agent Rush, Challenge 1: Blast Radius Zero.

The problem: websites are passive, insecure and not built for AI agents. Only about 15% of the world's websites are active. Search sends them fewer clicks, and customers now send AI agents to shop. WordPress runs 39.4% of all websites, and had 11,334 new vulnerabilities in 2025. A small business can't keep up.
Our solution: Agentrix WebAgent Platform turns a WordPress, Shopify or React website into an autonomous AI business, with WebAgents working 24/7 for the owner and the customer.

This is the home page for agentrix.website. Paste your website address for a free assessment, or watch the film to get an explanation of what Agentrix is. For a demo of an Agentrix website, here is Kilele Bakery, one of three businesses showcasing WebAgents. Each menu item is an AI WebAgent that does a specific task, and can share requests or orders with the site owner, Wanjiru, who approves anything that costs money. A customer asks: are you open on Sunday? The site answers from its own pages. Another asks for a 3 kilo cake for a 4 year old who loves Roblox. The cake creator turns the words into a cake from Kilele's own options, two tiers, chocolate, sky blue, priced at 4,850 shillings from the price list, and draws an image of it with AI. Wanjiru confirms every cake.

Here is the architecture, explained simply. A control server runs the websites and the agents, and plans and signs every job. A separate sandbox server does anything risky, inside sealed rooms with no secrets. One gateway talks to the AI models on Vultr, so no agent holds a key. Each agent wakes for a reason and proposes an action; a rule check allows it, holds it for the owner, or blocks it. Every action leaves a signed receipt.
Now let's run it live, on Zavora's own website. I paste the address. No account needed.
A real browser opens each page inside a sealed room on a separate Vultr server, takes screenshots, and checks it for errors and security problems.

In under a minute, the health report: hidden instructions aimed at AI assistants on three pages, and a hidden frame on the About page. The full report shows what the sealed browser saw, page by page, with the receipt for each room.

badge: Assess of Zavora's infected test site, on Vultr
beats.say: And on Zavora's infected test site: hidden spam links, a disguised script, and two pages that tried to send our sealed room somewhere it isn't allowed. Both were refused.

In plain words: the old site is never trusted. Every task is signed before it starts and receipted when it ends, so anyone can check it. Risky work runs in a sealed room with no passwords, thrown away afterwards. And ten real attacks planted in a hacked test site are scored from those receipts.

badge: a terminal, against the live site
beats.say: And in a terminal, this is what a customer's AI agent sees. The agent door lists what agents may do, and custom orders are held for the owner. The agent searches the catalogue over MCP, and asks a question with cited sources. Every action leaves a signed receipt, checkable against the site's published key.

The business is a subscription. Moving your site is free; you pay monthly for the WebAgents that run it, from twenty-nine dollars, through PayPal. It's for website owners, for agencies that run many client sites, and for developers who build on the platform.

What makes Agentrix different? Website builders make sites that wait. An Agentrix website is proactive, responsive and supportive at once, built on ADK-Rust: a kernel that keeps agents running, a harness that governs every action, real-time voice, memory, and a site engine that moves websites safely.
Made in Kenya, by the makers of ADK-Rust. We believe AGI is intelligent orchestration.
